ledger.claim: POL-NS-22 authorises a no-show cancellation fee of exactly 5.00 SGD, and POL-NS-26 fixes the no-show fee at 5.00 SGD. EV-FARE-05060 records a cancellation_fee of 6.50 SGD against a policy_fee_sgd of 5.00, and its own derived money block reports fee_matches_policy as false. The 1.50 SGD above the fixed fee was never an authorised charge against this rider, so no clause on this policy makes it a driver entitlement: the fee, at its highest, is the 5.00 SGD fee, and the excess is the rider's to keep. The driver's claim, which seeks the whole 6.50 SGD, cannot be granted on its face, and the amount mismatch calls for the POL-NS-22 referral, not a payment to the driver.

The driver's claim asks the Tribunal to restore to him the whole 6.50 SGD that the interim reversal already returned to the rider (fee_reversed, 2026-08-29T17:00:40+08:00). The figure the policy makes payable to a driver as no-show compensation is 5.00 SGD (POL-NS-22, POL-NS-26), and the record's charge never matched that figure (EV-FARE-05060, fee_matches_policy false). A claim that can only be satisfied at a sum above the fixed fee is not supported as filed, and POL-GEN-03's NO_ACTION - the party-relative outcome that leaves the present state standing and never restores a charge - is what follows: the rider keeps the reversal and is not put back on the charge.

POL-NS-24's driver-late test is keyed to the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes, and this record carries no scheduled time at all: EV-TRIP-05060's derived driver_deadline returns deadline null with the reason 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time'. POL-NS-24's own note directs that where the record carries none and the deadline cannot be fixed, POL-GEN-26 applies, so a fact that clause needs cannot be established from this record and the case belongs in human review, with the 6.50 SGD held rather than released to the driver (under POL-GEN-03 an escalated amount is held, not collected). I disclose that EV-ADVIS-05060-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY) is MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0; under POL-GEN-02(3) it carries no fact, and no third-party record is on file to supply the missing context either.

I do not contest the procedural preconditions, and the rider's case does not rest on them. EV-TRIP-05060's derived contact_before_cancel records a driver chat message at 14:09:40 and an in-app call placed at 14:12:10, both before the 14:15:40 cancellation, and EV-CHAT-05060 confirms both messages, so POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met. EV-GPS-05060's arrival_check corroborates the 14:09:15 arrival with a nearest fix 2.89 m from the pickup, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so POL-NS-21's free wait ran from a corroborated arrival and 385 s elapsed before cancellation. What the rider contests is the amount and the deadline the record leaves unfixed, not the wait or the contact.

Even if any part of the fee were to stand, POL-NS-25 is not engaged on this record: it operates only where rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is present and counts 3 or more, and the rider profile snapshot filed in this case (EV-RPROF-05060) carries no such counter. No repeat-no-show referral, mandatory upfront payment or suspension can follow from this trip, and the rider's account is not to be flagged on the strength of this charge.

The driver was physically at the pickup when he cancelled. The GPS trace's own arrival check records corroborated=true: the nearest fix sits 2.893 m from the pickup point at 14:09:55, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and inside the 25 m accuracy filter at a reported accuracy of 4.0 m, on a 25-fix trace with 100% coverage, a 30 s sample interval and no gap above 30 s (admissibility COMPLETE, weight 1.0). The arrival test under the no-show arrival rule is therefore satisfied on the platform's own code-computed facts, not on the driver's assertion.

The free wait was served in full and then some. Under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival, and on this record arrival is the marked event at 14:09:15, so the wait expired at 14:14:15; the driver cancelled at 14:15:40 — 385 s after arrival, 85 s after expiry. The precondition POL-NS-21 sets for a rider no-show cancellation is met, and no clause of the no-show policy requires a longer wait.

Both limbs of the driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 are satisfied, on the record, before the cancellation. The driver sent in-app chat messages at 14:09:40 ('Hi I at the pick up point Blk 670', read 14:10:29) and at 14:13:00 ('Hello?', read 14:13:35), and placed an in-app call at 14:12:10 that rang 30 s unanswered — every one of these events precedes the 14:15:40 cancellation. The derived contact check records obligation_met=true. POL-NS-23's premise for voiding the fee is therefore absent and it cannot supply a FULL_REFUND against the driver.

POL-NS-24 cannot be turned against the driver. That clause operates only where the driver fails to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes, and this was an on-demand booking with scheduled_at null — the record's own driver_deadline carries deadline=null for exactly that reason, so there is no deadline to miss; the clause's second limb fails too, because the driver both messaged and called. POL-GEN-26 is not engaged either: the missing deadline is a precondition this trip never had by design, not a fact the evidence failed to establish, so no open question is left for a human.

Because the driver cancelled after an expired free wait and had met the contact obligation, POL-NS-22 fixes the consequence: the no-show cancellation fee charged to the rider is transferred to the driver as compensation for his time and fuel. Where the fee stands the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the fee charged, so the money the ruling moves here is 6.50 SGD.

The amount charged (6.50 SGD) exceeds the 5.00 SGD the schedule sets, and POL-NS-22 resolves that discrepancy in the driver's favour: where the record charged an amount other than 5.00 SGD, the ruling acts on the amount charged and adds a referral naming that clause. Pol-GEN-03 confirms that such a fee-amount check produces a referral, not an escalation, and that referrals never suppress the money. The excess is therefore a referral item for the platform and is not a reason to void or reduce the driver's compensation.

The 6.50 SGD was taken from the driver only as an interim reversal 'pending review' after the rider complained (fee_reversed at 17:00:40), and the fare ledger confirms the present state: payment_status REFUNDED and refund_issued_sgd 6.50. NO_ACTION is party-relative and preserves that state, which here means the driver's claim fails and he keeps nothing for a wait the policy makes compensable. The outcome that matches the record is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 6.50 SGD, restoring the sum recovered from him.

EV-ADVIS-05060-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY) is MISSING — status MISSING, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0 — so it carries no fact at all (POL-GEN-02) and its absence cannot be used against the driver. No clause of the no-show policy makes a traffic advisory a required fact: POL-NS-21 requires trip_record and gps_trace, POL-NS-23 requires chat_log and trip_record, and POL-NS-22 requires fare_breakdown. Since POL-GEN-26 only escalates where a fact a rule needs cannot be established, and no no-show rule needs a traffic advisory, this absence supports no escalation and leaves the driver's entitlement intact.

Nothing stands in the way of a final monetary ruling now. The dispute value is 6.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD AI-final threshold, and fraud_flags is 0 on both the rider and the driver profile, so the 0.95 confidence bar is not engaged. POL-NS-26 confirms the AI ruling on a no-show is final subject only to safety, the fraud-flag bar and POL-GEN-26, none of which applies here. The driver's compensation should be issued rather than held on an escalation.

The rider's own counter-statement does not deny the no-show or the driver's contact; he says only that he was charged 'more than the $5 I know about' and that the refund was 'fine'. Nothing in the rider's account contradicts the timed record of arrival at 14:09:15, the wait, the 14:12:10 call and the two messages, so the only live question between the parties is the amount — which POL-NS-22 routes to a referral, not to the driver's detriment.

ruling.explanation:
To driver D-62878 and rider R-81472: the no-show stands, so the 6.50 SGD already taken back from the driver is payable to him. Driver: your claim is upheld. Rider: you keep nothing against the driver on this trip, but the overcharge point you raised is referred to the platform.

Driver, on the record: you marked arrival at the pickup at 14:09:15, and the GPS trace's own arrival check corroborates it (nearest fix 2.89 m from Block 670, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius and inside the 25 m accuracy filter, on a complete 25-fix trace). The 300 s free wait under POL-NS-21 therefore ran from 14:09:15 and expired at 14:14:15; you cancelled at 14:15:40, 385 s after arrival. You also met the contact obligation in POL-NS-23: in-app messages at 14:09:40 and 14:13:00, and an in-app call at 14:12:10, all before the cancellation. POL-NS-23 therefore cannot void the fee. Because the cancellation came after the free wait, POL-NS-22 makes the fee payable to you as compensation.

The money: EV-FARE-05060 records 6.50 SGD charged to the rider at 14:15:44 and then refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver at 17:00:40 'pending review'. The no-show being valid, that fee is owed to the driver: under POL-NS-22 the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with both amount fields equal to the amount charged, so 6.50 SGD is restored to you and the same 6.50 SGD is the figure this ruling moves.

Rider, your two arguments do not change that. (1) You say the fee can only be 5.00 SGD, not 6.50. POL-NS-22 addresses exactly this: the schedule fixes 5.00 SGD, but where the record charged an amount other than 5.00 SGD the ruling acts on the amount charged and adds a referral naming that clause. Your 1.50 SGD point is real and is the referral above; it reduces nothing the driver is paid. POL-NS-26's statement that the no-show fee is 5.00 SGD does not override POL-NS-22's own rule for a mismatched charge, and POL-GEN-03 confirms a fee-amount check produces a referral, not an escalation. Your own statement (you were charged 6.50 SGD and 'then it was refunded, fine') concedes the no-show and does not contest the driver's contact. (2) You ask for human review under POL-NS-24 / POL-GEN-26. POL-NS-24's driver-late test is keyed to a scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes, and this was an on-demand booking with scheduled_at null — the record's own driver_deadline is null for that reason, the driver in fact arrived and was corroborated, and you never cancelled. Nothing this case needs is missing or impaired: the trip record is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and the absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05060-01, MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) carries no fact and is required by no no-show clause. POL-GEN-26 is therefore not engaged and the amount is not held.

POL-NS-25 is not engaged: the rider profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter, so no repeat no-show referral or account flag follows from this trip. The dispute value is 6.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD AI-final threshold; fraud_flags are 0 on both profiles and there is no safety flag, so this ruling is final.

Confidence 0.90. The facts this ruling rests on — arrival, free wait, contact, and the fee amount — are carried by EV-TRIP-05060, EV-GPS-05060, EV-CHAT-05060 and EV-FARE-05060, each at weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
referrals: POL-NS-22: the record charged a 6.50 SGD no-show fee (EV-FARE-05060, fee_matches_policy false), an amount other than the 5.00 SGD the schedule fixes; the platform should review the fee amount charged to the rider.
